title: Meghalaya Records 60% Monsoon Rainfall Deficit Amid El Nino Conditions - Northeast Today
article_text:
Meghalaya has experienced a severe 60 per cent rainfall deficit this monsoon, largely attributed to the ongoing El Niño phenomenon. Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma stated on Tuesday that despite the shortfall, early rains at the beginning of the season helped the state manage better. He emphasized that the government has taken proactive steps, including the formulation of a comprehensive water policy and satellite mapping of nearly 17,000 springs, to mitigate the impact of erratic weather patterns.
A recent study has warned that the prevailing “super El Niño” conditions over the equatorial Pacific are expected to intensify into a very strong event, lasting until February 2027. This could result in approximately 15,800 additional heat-related deaths in India over the next six months compared to a normal year. Experts also caution that foodgrain production, particularly during the upcoming Rabi season in rainfed regions, may be adversely affected.Explore History
